content: Lamivudine and zidovudine can suppress your body’s ability to produce sufficient blood cells. Inform your doctor if you currently have or have ever had blood disorders such as anemia or bone marrow issues. If you experience symptoms like unusual bleeding or bruising, shortness of breath, pale skin, fever, sore throat, chills, signs of infection, or unusual fatigue or weakness, contact your doctor immediately. These medications may also cause muscle disorders. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had muscle diseases or swelling. If you experience muscle pain or weakness, seek medical attention promptly. When used alone or in combination with other antiretroviral drugs, lamivudine and zidovudine can cause severe liver damage and a condition called lactic acidosis. Inform your doctor if you consume or have consumed large amounts of alcohol or if you have or have had liver disease. Additionally, let your doctor and pharmacist know if you are taking acetaminophen (Tylenol) or have been on long-term HIV treatment. If you experience symptoms such as fatty or foul-smelling stools, stomach upset, extreme fatigue, unusual bleeding or bruising, lack of energy, loss of appetite, pain in the upper right abdomen, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or flu-like symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. It is essential to keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific tests to monitor your body’s response to lamivudine and zidovudine. The combination of lamivudine and zidovudine is prescribed to treat human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in patients with or without acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). These drugs belong to a class of antiviral medications called synthetic nucleoside analogues, which work by slowing the spread of HIV in the body. However, they are not a cure for HIV and may not reduce the number of HIV-related illnesses. They also do not prevent the transmission of HIV to others. Lamivudine and zidovudine are available as oral tablets, typically taken twice daily with or without food. To ensure consistent use, take the medication at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking lamivudine and zidovudine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to lamivudine (Epivir, Epivir HBV), zidovudine (Retrovir), or any other medications. Be aware that lamivudine and zidovudine are also available individually under the brand names Epivir, Epivir HBV, and Retrovir, and in another combination as Trizivir. Inform your doctor if you are taking any of these medications to avoid receiving the same drug twice. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Mention specific drugs such as acetaminophen (Tylenol), acyclovir (Zovirax), atovaquone (Mepron), cancer chemotherapy drugs, cidofovir (Vistide), dapsone (Avlosulfon), didanosine (ddI, Videx), doxorubicin (Adriamycin, Rubex), fluconazole (Diflucan), foscarnet (Foscavir), ganciclovir (Cytovene, Vitrasert), interferon alpha (Alferon N, Infergen, Intron A, Roferon A), interferon beta-1b (Betaseron), methadone, nelfinavir (Viracept), probenecid (Benemid, Probalan), ribavirin (Rebetol, Virazole), rifabutin (Mycobutin), rifampin (Rifadin, Rimactane), ritonavir (Norvir), stavudine (Zerit), trimethoprim (Trimpex, Proloprim), trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim, Septra), valproic acid (Depakene, Depakote), and zalcitabine (ddC, Hivid). Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. In addition to the conditions listed in the Important Warning section, inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney disease. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking lamivudine and zidovudine, contact your doctor. Do not breastfeed while on this medication. Be aware that your body fat may increase or redistribute to areas such as your breasts or upper back. Unless directed otherwise by your doctor, continue your normal diet. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Lamivudine and zidovudine may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: headache, upset stomach, diarrhea, constipation, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, excessive tiredness, depression, stuffy nose, cough, or hair loss. Some side effects can be serious. If you experience hives, skin rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, seizures, numbness or tingling in your fingers or toes, fever, or wheezing, contact your doctor immediately. Report any unusual problems while taking this medication to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Inform your doctor and lab personnel that you are taking lamivudine and zidovudine before undergoing any tests. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
